A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same distributional-discrepancy defense, renamed from DDAD to DAD. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K defense experiments, transfer-attack results, ablations and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark, transfer and ablation results and adds a regularization-weight sensitivity experiment in Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: The optimized MMD statistic, DUNET denoiser, Gaussian noise, combined MMD/cross-entropy objective and threshold-based inference remain unchanged. Renaming DDAD to DAD and relocating or abbreviating Algorithms 1–3 do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K with the same adversarial-classification, transfer-attack and mixed-batch scenarios. The changed sensitivity experiments vary parameters within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and adversarial-training combination tables retain the same comparators. Wu et al. (2020) remains TRADES-AWP in the combination table; v2's prose calling it MART does not establish a different evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a CIFAR-10 experiment varying α over 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10, while removing the ImageNet threshold sweep from 0.010 to 0.050. Existing benchmark protocols, attack budgets, training settings and default parameter choices remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ablation testing sensitivity to the cross-entropy loss weight α, but removes the ImageNet MMD-OPT threshold-sensitivity analysis in v1 Table 7. The CIFAR-10 threshold, batch-size, mixed-batch, Gaussian-noise and two-pronged-process analyses remain.

E5.justification: Retained experiments preserve their reporting practices, including five-run CIFAR-10 and three-run ImageNet means and standard deviations. Both the removed threshold table and added α table report point estimates without additional uncertainty or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: All eleven retained result tables match numerically after relocation and renumbering. New v2 Table 7 reports robust accuracies of 67.53%, 50.70% and 45.35% as α increases, with clean accuracy fixed at 94.16%. Removed v1 Table 7 showed ImageNet robustness falling from 53.75% at threshold 0.025 to 0.46% at 0.030–0.050.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the K-class label and hypothesis codomains from {0, 1, ..., K} to {1, ..., K}, eliminating an extra label. The assumptions, binary-classification definitions, Theorem 1, Appendix A proof and MMD mathematics otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that distributional discrepancy motivates a defense combining denoising guidance and adversarial detection, preserving inputs and improving clean and robust accuracy. The new title and 'one stone, two birds' framing emphasize roles already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new α ablation as showing that weakening MMD-OPT's relative influence reduces robustness, linking this observation to Section 3. It also changes 'can help reduce' to 'can directly reduce' in the theoretical discussion. Existing batching, latency and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2's abstract newly states that code is publicly available and provides a project repository address. V1 lacks this access information. Detailed implementation settings, hardware, training times and inference times are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. (2021a) on meta two-sample testing and discussions of Zhou et al. (2023a, 2023b), while removing Sharif et al. (2016) and Jing et al. (2021). Positioning relative to detection, adversarial training and purification remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, renames DDAD to DAD, revises the abstract and contribution presentation, introduces theory subsections and adds acknowledgements. Algorithms and transfer results move into the main text. These are targeted revisions within a largely retained narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and relabelled, Algorithms 1–3 become main-text column-width displays, and the unchanged transfer table moves from the appendix to the main text. The α table replaces the removed ImageNet threshold table, with accompanying table relocation and reflow; Figure 2 retains its findings.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful α-sensitivity evidence, code-access information and more accessible algorithm presentation. However, deleting v1 Table 7 removes important evidence of ImageNet robustness collapsing from 53.75% to 0.46% after a small threshold increase, while the threshold-selection discussion remains. With the main results unchanged, these benefits and the loss of failure-boundary evidence leave the net quality change uncertain.
